title: What is known about 1RB0LB_0RC0LF_1LD1RE_0LA0RB_0RD0RF_0LA---
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0LB_0RC0LF_1LD1RE_0LA0RB_0RD0RF_0LA---.
intro: This six-state machine is a holdout of the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on: the structure of its run (two counters ticking together), the rules proved in Lean, and the open question.
verdict: The question is open. The machine is a rewriting system on the right half of its tape (the visit law, proved in Lean): it halts only if a visit meets 111. Its first four rules are those of the three machines that busycoq PR59 proves to halt in round 161,211 on the block 1011; this machine rewrites 1011 to 0001 instead and, in an accelerated run (computed, not proved), carries on: no halt up to round 200,000. No halt in the first 1011 steps of a direct run.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: The sweeps of the run
claims.text: The shift rules the machine uses in its run (every sweep met when the symbolic simulator runs from many configurations of the run), each for every number of copies.

claims.title: Both counters' increments, for all sizes
claims.text: At an event (A on cell 3), the same 9 theorems as the reference 1RB0LB_0RC0LD_1LD1RE_0LA0RF_0RD1RB_0RC--- (proved here again for this machine): At an event (A on cell 3): the left increment with a carry over n ones (12n+24 steps), the right increment on a lowest 0 (28 steps) and with a carry over k+1 ones three cells apart (8k+36 steps), with the engine block plain or marked, and carries crossing junk units 1010000, which they leave unchanged (one unit; j units in a row, 24j+36 steps; j units and then k+1 more ones, 24j+8k+44 steps). Plus y_e1_detour: L E> 1 0 R reaches L 1 B> 0 R in 3 steps (E1 = 0RF, F0 = 0LA, A0 = 1RB), where the reference's E1 = 1RB takes 1.

claims.title: The visit law: the machine as a rewriting system
claims.text: A visit (the head enters a stream s in state C with a 0 on its left and returns in state A two cells further left) rewrites the stream by 0 s → 1 s, 100 s → 000 v(s), 110 s → 000 v(s), 1010 s → 1010 v(v(s)), 1011 s → 0001 s, for every stream and every tape to the left. 111 s halts the machine. The six prefixes 0, 100, 110, 111, 1010 and 1011 cover every stream, so these rules are the whole machine: it can halt only when a visit meets 111. From blank tape the run is a sequence of rounds 0∞ A> 1 0 S → 0∞ A> 1 0 v(1 0 S), starting from S = 1 0∞ after 4 steps.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 252 cells have been visited and 74 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>11</sup> steps
claims.text: A direct run of 1011 steps (longrun.c, the simulator of tools/c/tm.h) without a halt.

claims.title: The left side is clockwork
claims.text: Between consecutive left-end extensions the busiest cell turns exactly 2<sup>k</sup> times, each power twice (64, 64, 128, 128, ..., 2<sup>24</sup>), in the first 1.5·10<sup>9</sup> steps.

claims.title: E1 is rare
claims.text: E1 is used 306 times in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps; every other non-halting transition 10<sup>7</sup> to 2·10<sup>8</sup> times.

claims.title: How much of the run the increments cover
claims.text: In the first 108 steps (1,048,574 events) 95.2% of the events are instances of these theorems (left 524,258; right0 262,133; right1 92,325; junk_10 78,635; junk_110 39,313; junk_jk 1,733; right1m 9; right0m 1). The other 50,167 are carries over junk layouts the rules do not list (two junk stretches, junk words other than 1010000) and the moments around left-end visits. The event tapes are the reference's (first 2,000,000 events compared); each event comes 2 steps later per earlier use of E1 (498 = 2 × 249).

claims.title: It does not halt where the PR59 machines halt
claims.text: The first four rules are also the rules of the three machines that busycoq PR59 proves to halt (they halt on 1011, in round 161,211). An accelerated simulator of the visit law (counts of visits kept as 2e − c; rules learned from the table; checked against a direct run, against exact integers for 1,500 rounds, and against PR59's halting round on the reference machine) finds: rounds 1 to 161,210 use only the four shared rules, round 161,211 meets 1011 at the right end of the word, writes 0001 and continues. Observed: no halt and no visit to 111 up to round 200,000. Computed, not proved.

claims.title: Growth shape: exp/exp
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.073). Right of the start it grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.067).

claims.title: Two counters of the same events
claims.text: Read off the run: the counters on the two sides of the engine both go up by 1 at every visit of the head to the engine, one of them with fixed junk stretches between some digits; the junk is written when a carry reaches the end of the tape.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. It halts only if F reads a 1, i.e. only if after B1 (0LF) and E1 (0RF) the head finds a 1; it never has, and the layout of the junk, which would decide it, is not decoded.

claims.title: Related holdouts
claims.text: The same tapes at another pace, whatever the states, as 4 other holdouts (listed on the explainer page).

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. This machine is a small rewriting system: blocks 000/100 that act as binary digits and blocks 1010 that double the visits passing through. Three sister machines with the same four rules are proved to halt in round 161,211 on the block 1011; this one rewrites that block and runs on.

facts.text: The visit law: the machine as a rewriting system on streams.
No halt in the accelerated run; the PR59 machines halt in round 161,211.
No halt in a direct run.
Turns of the busiest cell between left-end extensions.

sections.eyebrow: The whole machine in a few rules
sections.heading: The visit law
html: Forget the states for a moment. Call everything from some cell to the right a stream. Whenever the head steps into a stream in state C with a 0 behind it, it comes back out in state A two cells further left, and the only thing that has changed is the stream. That excursion is a visit, and what it does depends only on how the stream begins (proved in Lean for every stream):

the stream beginsafter the visitLean
0 s1 svis_0
100 s000 then one visit to svis_100
110 s000 then one visit to svis_110
1010 s1010 then two visits to svis_1010
1011 s0001 svis_1011
111 sthe machine haltsvis_111_halts

So a block 000/100 is a binary digit: it passes every second visit on. A block 1010 is a doubler: it passes every visit on twice. 111 s halts the machine. The six prefixes 0, 100, 110, 111, 1010 and 1011 cover every stream, so these rules are the whole machine: it can halt only when a visit meets 111.

The run from blank tape is a sequence of rounds: the tape is 0∞ A> 1 0 S, and one round puts 1 0 in front of S and makes one visit. After k rounds S begins with k copies of 10, that is k/2 doublers, so 2k/2 visits reach the word behind them. That word is the right-hand counter of the earlier descriptions.

The same rules, a different ending. The three machines that busycoq PR59 proves to halt have the same first four rules; they halt when a visit meets 1011, which first happens in round 161,211. This machine writes 0001 there instead. In our accelerated run (computed, checked three ways, not proved) it does exactly that in round 161,211 and carries on; no halt up to round 200,000.

sections.heading: Two counters and an engine
html:
Most of the time the tape is L · engine · R. Each visit of the head to the engine is an event, and every event adds 1 to both counters. In the reference machine of the family (1RB0LB_0RC0LD_1LD1RE_0LA0RF_0RD1RF_0RC---), L is written in blocks of four cells, 0101 for a 1 and 0001 for a 0, lowest digit next to the engine, and R keeps one cell per digit, three cells apart (the cells 9, 12, 15, … right of the head), lowest digit nearest the engine. Nine consecutive events of the reference machine right after its left-end visit at step 1,571,372 (the head in state A on the bold cell):

(The block of L touching the engine is always 0001; the low bits shown are the next three blocks. The carries are sweeps proved in Lean for every length; in the reference machine r_up and r_down carry the right counter over k ones in 5k + 13 and 3k + 18 steps.)

This machine is a disguised copy (B1 = 0LF with F0 = 0LA, so F reading 0 acts as D; D1 = 0RB; E1 = 0RF): the same left-end extensions to within a few hundred steps, and E1 rare.

sections.heading: The left side is clockwork
html:
When L overflows, the carry runs to the left end of the tape, the tape grows by two cells there, and L starts again. The lowest digit of L is the cell where the head turns most often, and the number of its turns between two consecutive left-end extensions follows a strict pattern, without a single exception in the first 1.5·109 steps (ymax.c):

64 64 128 128 256 256 512 512 … 223 223 224

So the periods of the left side are powers of two in events, each length twice (the counter gains one digit every two periods). The time per event is not constant, because a carry on the right costs more when it crosses junk, so the steps between left-end extensions grow by factors between about 1.35 and 2.05 instead of exactly 2.

sections.heading: A counter with junk between its digits
html: The cells that change between events are the digits of the counters: each digit changes about half as often as the one before (chg.c counts, over a whole period, how often each cell changes from one event to the next). On the right, between some digits of R, there are stretches of fixed cells (0101010101 00 1 00 1 00 1 and the like) that the carries cross without changing. They are written when a carry runs into the end of the tape, at irregular event counts, and their layout is what makes the run irregular. How they are produced is not decoded yet.

sections.heading: The dangerous moments
html: The machine halts only in state F reading a 1, and F is entered from B1 (0LF) and E1 (0RF). After B1, used about 4·107 times in 109 steps, the head has read a 0 every time. E1 is the rare one: 306 uses in 109 steps, each followed by a 0, as in the reference machine, where in the reference machine E1 fires when a carry of the right counter reaches a digit for the first time since the last left-end visit: right after the visit at step 2,188,604 it fires at steps 2,188,675, 2,188,767, 2,188,882, 2,189,117, 2,189,592, 2,190,547, 2,192,462, three cells further right each time and after twice the wait each time, as a binary counter reaching new digits. None of this has happened; whether the junk can ever arrange it is the open question.

sections.heading: Eight machines, one mechanism
html: The family (G11-Y): 1RB0LB_0RC0LD_1LD1RE_0LA0RF_0RD1RF_0RC--- (the reference), 1RB0LB_0RC0LD_1LD1RE_0LA0RF_0RD1RB_0RC--- (the same run), 1RB0LB_0RC0LD_1LD1RE_0LA0RF_0RD0LC_0RC---, 1RB0LB_0RC0LD_1LD1RE_0LA0RF_1RB0RD_0RB---, 1RB0LB_0RC0LF_1LD1RE_0LA0RB_0RD0RF_0LA--- (all with left-end extensions after 2k events, each twice, to within a few hundred steps of each other); 1RB0LB_0RC0LE_1RD0RF_1LB1RB_0LA0RE_1RE--- and 1RB0LB_0RC0LE_1RD0RF_1LB1RB_0LA1RB_1RE--- (the same right part, a differently written left counter); and the mirror case 1RB0LB_0RC0LD_1LD1RE_0LA0RB_0RD1RF_1LA---, with the junk on the left.

sections.heading: The increments, proved for every size
html: Every visit of the head to the engine (A on cell 3) adds 1 to one of the two counters, and the theorems in lean/Events.lean prove each kind of visit for every size: they are the reference machine's theorems, unchanged. State F here plays the part of the reference's D after B reads a 1, and E1 takes a three-step detour (y_e1_detour) that ends where the reference's one step ends: the run passes through the reference's tapes.

sections.heading: What would settle it
html: Decode what a carry writes when it reaches the end of the tape, as a function of the counters, so that the layout of the junk after each visit is a formula. Then the question becomes whether a carry can ever find a 1 where it has always found a 0, which may be provable by an invariant of the junk, or may reduce to an arithmetic question about the two counters.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.073). Right of the start it grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.067).
After 109 steps the tape spans 252 cells (88 left of the start, 153 right), with a density of 1s of 0.294.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: Related machines
html: Other holdouts of the list of 608 that are tied to this one. The comparison of tables is exact; everything about runs was checked on the first 107 steps of each machine and is an observation, not a proof (holdouts/related.py, holdouts/related.json).

Same tapes at another pace (observed, not proved). Leave the states aside and compare only the tape and the place of the head. Then a large part of the first 107 configurations of this machine are configurations of the machines below, in the same order and up to the end of the run. The steps at which they occur differ, the tables are not renamings of each other, and equal tapes with different states may be continued differently, so this does not tie the halting questions together.

  • 1RB0LB_0RC0LD_1LD1RE_0LA0RF_0RD1RB_0RC---: 9,999,705 configurations, the last at step 10,000,000 here and step 9,999,704 there
  • 1RB0LB_0RC0LD_1LD1RE_0LA0RF_0RD1RF_0RC---: 9,999,705 configurations, the last at step 10,000,000 here and step 9,999,704 there

summary: A rewriting system on streams (visit law, proved in Lean): the first four rules are those of the PR59 machines that halt on 1011 in round 161,211; this one rewrites 1011 to 0001 and runs on (computed: no halt up to round 200,000); it halts only if a visit meets 111; open.
family: PR59 visit law (0, 100, 110, 1010 shared with the machines proved to halt; 1011 -> 0001)
